title: Type Lab
description: From browsing a font to exporting a type system: pairing, variable axes, fluid scales and previews from shared inputs.
techStack: Next.js, TypeScript, Variable Fonts, CSS, Design Tokens
status: Type Lab release merged; live web application

blocks.heading: A typography decision needs somewhere to go
blocks.body: Kern began as a variable-font explorer. Type Lab extends the workflow: browse the catalogue, choose heading, body and mono roles, compare them in interface previews, tune a fluid scale and export the result. The output matters as much as the specimen.

blocks.heading: Follow a type decision into production

steps.label: Catalogue boundary
steps.detail: A server-side fetch races the live refresh against a patience window. The browser can receive the bundled catalogue while an upstream request completes into the cache.

steps.label: Type roles
steps.detail: Heading, body and mono share one lab state. The same family can serve more than one role without requiring duplicate font requests.

steps.label: Scale mathematics
steps.detail: Each step has two endpoint sizes, a slope and an intercept. Tracking tightens with size; leading is derived from the base. Rounding happens when formatting output.

steps.label: Export boundary
steps.detail: CSS, Tailwind v4 and token output receive the same roles and scale. Browser-measured fallback faces feed size-adjust rather than changing the authored font sizes.

blocks.caption: The path is from source data to an editable design-system artefact. It is separate from a claim about which typeface improves conversion or readability.

blocks.heading: Make the catalogue resilient
blocks.context: The catalogue should refresh without requiring every visitor to wait for an upstream service.

options.label: Only serve a live catalogue
options.detail: Fresh data, but a slow or changed upstream response blocks the first useful screen.

options.label: Live metadata with a bundled fallback
options.detail: Try the keyless Google Fonts metadata endpoint, then the official API when configured, then a bundled snapshot. A short patience window lets the page return the snapshot while refresh continues.

blocks.outcome: Source selection is explicit in lib/catalogue/fetch.ts. The snapshot can also be rebuilt deliberately, rather than relying on a hand-maintained font list.

blocks.heading: Pairing with reasons
blocks.body: Suggestions combine category contrast, curated pairings and font measurements where available. Each suggestion carries its reasons. They are typography heuristics, not a model predicting which pairing will perform best. Variable axes use each font’s actual range rather than assuming every family exposes the same controls.

blocks.heading: One system behind the previews and exports
blocks.context: A good-looking preview is misleading if copying the output produces different typography.

options.label: Calculate each export independently
options.detail: Easy to start, but the preview, CSS and token output can drift.

options.label: Generate from shared role and scale inputs
options.detail: Use the same heading, body and mono state, catalogue entries and scale steps for CSS, Tailwind and token exports.

blocks.outcome: Scale arithmetic keeps full precision until formatting. Both ends of the viewport range define the fluid interpolation. Interface previews make the pairing reviewable in context.

blocks.heading: Be explicit about fluid tokens
blocks.gave: A fluid clamp() value cannot be represented as a single standard DTCG dimension.
blocks.got: Each scale step exports minimum and maximum typography tokens. A namespaced extension carries the clamp() expression for tools that understand it; consumers still need to implement the interpolation.

blocks.heading: A route for each part of the job
blocks.body: The root is now the font browser. Pairing, the scale and export have their own routes; the traditional specimen is at /specimen. Sources for the shared implementation are lib/scale.ts, lib/export.ts, lib/pairing.ts and lib/catalogue/fetch.ts. No adoption or performance outcome is claimed here.
